lessons: Keep hooks extremely direct and concise: the highest performing retention at 10% (such as the Greenland shark video) starts immediately with a bold, high-stakes claim without fluff.

Avoid descriptive framing or lengthy multi-clause hook lines in the first 10 seconds, as clips with overly descriptive intros (e.g., Maple Syrup or Potatoes) see massive early drop-offs exceeding 30%.
Eliminate repetitive phrasing or immediate redundancy in early explanation lines; the potato video showed identical drops due to repeating text, causing immediate viewer fatigue.
Structure the core explanation without pacing lags around the 25% to 50% mark, where sharp drops consistently occur if the script slows down its delivery.

Focus topics on extreme physical contrasts or biological anomalies (like the Greenland shark or Tuna vs. Cod), which maintain significantly higher end-retention and sustained viewer engagement compared to everyday food facts.
worst_moment_types: Multi-clause introductory sentences that over-explain the premise before establishing high stakes
Slow transitional explanations around the 25% to 40% timeline that stall momentum
Repetitive information or redundant phrasing in early script lines
Abrupt pauses or low-energy delivery right after the hook
best_hook_types: High-stakes declarative statements about extreme biological survival or longevity
Short, punchy contrarian facts that challenge common assumptions immediately
